subject: Categorical data: summarising counts in contingency tables, testing them with chi-square tests, describing an association with relative risk and odds ratios, and spotting Simpson's paradox
outOfScope: The logic of hypothesis tests, p-values and errors (see the Hypothesis testing pack)
Comparing two proportions with a z-test and pooled proportion (see the Comparing groups pack); this pack only notes that a 2 × 2 chi-square equals its Z squared
Conditional probability and the multiplication rule in depth (see the Probability distributions pack); Bayes' theorem (see the Bayesian inference pack)
Confidence intervals for a relative risk or an odds ratio, and their log-scale standard errors
Exact tests (Fisher's exact test), likelihood-ratio (G) tests, McNemar's test for paired proportions and tests for ordinal tables, beyond naming them
Three-way tables in depth: Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel tests, conditional independence and log-linear models
Logistic regression and the odds ratio as a model coefficient (see the Classification metrics pack for classifiers)
Formulas and derivations, and the multinomial and Poisson sampling models behind the tests
Tooling: Minitab, R, Python, StatKey and spreadsheet functions

concepts.title: Simpson's paradox
concepts.outcome: Recognise when combining groups reverses an association, and look for the third variable responsible.

keyPoints.text: An observed association between two variables can change or even reverse direction when another variable interacts strongly with both of them.
